s1.syndrome_frame: Enlarging, painful, purplish mass in the ear canal with granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells
salient_findings: Purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal
Irregular, friable surface with bleeding on minimal contact
Lobulated mass extending into the external acoustic canal and parotid space
Bilateral cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm in diameter
key_facts: 7-year-old girl
2-year history of enlarging mass
Intermittent pain
Purplish lump in left ear canal
Cracking and pus-filled sores at the site 18 months prior
Received antibiotics and analgesics
3.5 × 2.5 cm mass in left external ear canal
Mass has irregular, friable surface
Bleeding on minimal contact
Contrast-enhanced CT showed lobulated mass in cutis and subcutis
Mass extends into external acoustic canal and parotid space
Bilateral level II–IV cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm
CT angiography demonstrated marked vascularity
Incisional biopsy revealed atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor with rapid growth, matching the 2-year history of enlarging mass and presence of atypical cells

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of atypical cells, consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Marked vascularity of the mass and presence of atypical cells, consistent with angiosarcoma

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor with rapid growth, matching the 2-year history of enlarging mass and presence of atypical cells

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral level II-IV cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm, suggesting lymphoma involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of a rapidly enlarging, painful, and bleeding mass in a child, along with the imaging findings of a lobulated mass with marked vascularity and the biopsy results showing atypical cells, is most consistent with Rhabdomyosarcoma, a common soft tissue sarcoma in children.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple lesions and systemic symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: More common in adults and typically presents with cutaneous lesions, not a deep-seated mass like in this case.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a more systemic illness and a distinct 'onion-skin' appearance on imaging, not seen here.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Would typically present with more pronounced lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, not consistent with the localized mass in this case.
